title: Regression runbook and weekly signal snapshot — Sprint 16
content:
Objective:
This runbook captures the weekly snapshot for model onboarding regressions (Sprint 16). It focuses on promptset-level failures discovered by the onboarding eval harness, a quick triage of top signals, immediate mitigations we pushed, and actionable owners for next-week work. The doc is intentionally lightweight — use it for async handoffs and to centralize quick hypotheses and owners.

TL;DR (top-line):
- Signal: overall pass-rate for new model candidate 'redwood-open-3b-v2' fell from 94% to 87% on our onboarding promptsets over the past 7 days.
- Largest drift concentrated in the FAQ and support prompt families (prefix mismatches + hallucination on dates).
- Top 3 failure modes: hallucinated facts, instruction-following failures (missing required fields), and truncation/early-stops on long-context replies.
- Immediate mitigations: rolled back tokenizer patch on staging, tightened stop-sequence heuristics for affected routes, added temporary reroute to fallback-v1 for high-risk customers.

Key metrics (last 7 days vs prior 7 days):
- Overall onboarding pass-rate: 87% (was 94%)
- Median latency (inference): 120ms -> 132ms (small increase after kernel tweak)
- Hallucination rate (per promptset sampling): 6.3% -> 10.8%
- Critical failures (customer-impacting): 14 -> 29
- Sticky promptsets (most failing): support-faq, policy-summarization, legal-extractors

Top 5 failure modes (with short reproducible notes):
1) Hallucinated dates/locations in extraction tasks
   - Example: prompt expects "date_of_event" from text blob; model invented 2021 when source says 2019.
   - Signal path: policy-summarization and support-faq promptsets.
   - Hypothesis: quantization knob + recent tokenization tweak caused subtle token misalignment for multi-digit sequences.

2) Missing required fields for structured outputs
   - Example: schema requires 'summary' + 'highlights'; model returns only 'summary'.
   - Signal path: legal-extractors and enterprise-onboard promptsets.
   - Hypothesis: beam/temperature defaults changed with new runtime that favors shorter outputs.

3) Early-stop on long-context completions
   - Example: truncates after 3rd paragraph when 6 are expected.
   - Signal path: longform-note-taking promptset.
   - Hypothesis: KV-cache eviction threshold lowered; cache miss leads to shorter continuation.

4) Instruction override (model follows system prompt but ignores user constraint)
   - Example: user asked to not include examples; model injected examples.
   - Signal path: tutorial and examples prompt families.
   - Hypothesis: model attention re-weighting change after kernel selection change.

5) Tokenization mismatch for code blocks causing parse errors
   - Example: returned code contains stray control characters, breaks downstream parsers.
   - Signal path: developer-tools promptset.
   - Hypothesis: tokenizer mapping for backticks changed in recent patch.

Promptset hotlist (priority tags for triage):
- P0: support-faq, policy-summarization
- P1: legal-extractors, enterprise-onboard
- P2: longform-note-taking, developer-tools

Triage notes and quick checks performed this week:
- Reproduced hallucination on 8/10 seed examples locally under quantized runtime; non-quantized baseline passed. (Ethan L.)
- A/B test between kernel v12 and v11 shows latency tradeoff and small increase in hallucination for v12. (Perf bench linked in artifacts).
- Tokenization diffs captured by small-script diff-tokenmap.py; backticks normalization changed. (Marta K.)

Immediate mitigations applied (what we changed in prod/staging):
- Reverted tokenizer normalization patch on staging (rolled back June 10). Status: staging pass-rate +4pt. Owner: Marta Kovac.
- Added route-level fallback policy: if promptset==support-faq and hallucination_score>threshold => route to fallback-v1. Owner: Samir Patel.
- Lowered default temperature for enterprise-onboard route from 0.8 -> 0.6. Owner: Priya Shah.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- A1: Deep rootcause: run token-alignment compare across quantized and float runs (Ethan L) — due 2026-06-17.
- A2: Create promptset augmentation to include negative examples for hallucination (Marta K) — due 2026-06-21.
- A3: Add synthetic long-context regression harness for longform-note-taking (Samir P) — due 2026-06-20.
- A4: Draft customer comms template for any SLA-impacting regressions and coordinate with CS (Priya S, CS lead) — due 2026-06-18.
- A5: Kernel rollback experiment: run 24h canary on 10% of production traffic comparing v11 vs v12 for hallucination + latency, feed to Optimize recommendations (Perf SRE) — due 2026-06-19.

Investigation hypotheses to prioritize (short list):
- H1: Quantization path changes + recent tokenizer tweak caused numeric token misalignment -> hallucinations on dates/numbers.
- H2: Kernel selection heuristics bias toward faster-but-shorter decode trajectories, increasing early-stops.
- H3: Model variant used for onboarding has different stop-token handling; prompt-engineering mismatch with updated system prompt.

Data & artifacts to consult (where you'll find the evidence):
- Confluence experiment page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/AI-REG-345
- Triage DAG: JIRA-APML-842
- Onboarding eval runs (raw): s3://redwood-evals/onboard/sprint-16/ (note: storage link, request access via infra ticket)
- PR with tokenizer change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-evals/pull/219

Long-term recommendations (post-sprint work):
- Harden onboarding harness: add cross-quantization consistency checks (float vs 8-bit) and expose per-token alignment diffs in dashboards.
- Add prompt-level acceptance criteria metadata (expected_verbs, required_fields, max_hallucination_rate) so gates can automatically fail unsafe rollouts.
- Expand synthetic negative prompt generation for hallucination detection across numeric patterns and date formats (multi-locale).
- Invest in deterministic stop-token tests in CI for long-context decoders.

Risks and customer impact summary:
- Risk: If rollout continues unchecked, enterprise customers using legal-extractors could receive incomplete or incorrect extractions leading to downstream contract errors.
- Mitigation: route-critical customers to dedicated capacity or fallback-v1 until pass-rate recovers above 92%.

Notes to reviewers / quick asks:
- Please add any missing failing promptset names to the hotlist as you triage.
- If you pick up an action item, update the Jira ticket and add a one-line daily status in the ticket.
- For any kernel rollback experiment, coordinate with SRE and infra; we must preserve the rollback toggle in the rollout config.

Appendix (quick reproducibility recipes):
- Reproduce hallucination locally:
  1) Checkout branch token-fix-repro (github PR 219)
  2) Run python reproduce.py --promptset support-faq --seed 42 --quantized True --shots 5
  3) Compare output against baseline: python diff_outputs.py baseline.json out.json

- Quick console queries:
  - Query failing promptsets: SELECT promptset, count(*) FROM eval_runs WHERE outcome='fail' AND created_at >= '2026-06-07' GROUP BY promptset ORDER BY count DESC;

Acknowledgements: thanks to Ethan for perf runs, Marta for token diffs, Samir for mitigation rollout, and CS for early customer flags.

Revision history:

- 2026-06-14: updated metrics after staging revert (Priya Shah)
